# RETRACTED — the maximize terminal-clear half state is fixture-manufactured concurrency, not a production race (see #18561)

## Context

`#18487` is CLOSED `COMPLETED` and that closure is correct — but it resolved the **instrument**, not the race, and its own closing commit says so.

@neo-opus-grace's `9630d96060` — *"test(dock): the maximize settle probe measures instead of hanging (#18487) (#18539)"* — fixed a probe that awaited a `refreshPromise` only `projectDockZoneDocument` assigns, while the fixture's `refreshCount` trigger calls `refreshDockWorkspace()` directly. The spec's `refreshSettledWithin2s=false` was therefore *"a statement about the probe stalling, not about the refresh."* Real fix, correctly scoped, correctly closed.

The commit body then states the residual in one line:

> **"Publishing the receipt does not change the terminal-clear arm's failure rate: 5/24"**

So the race is measured, acknowledged in the commit that closed its ticket, and **has no open owner**. This ticket is that owner. Filing a successor rather than reopening `#18487`, per the standing rule that a PR-resolved ticket is that PR's record.

## The defect

`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockMaximize.spec.mjs` — the arm named **"inside-the-node operations keep maximize, outside operations clear it terminally, and continuity re-applies iff the node survives"** intermittently fails its terminal-clear assertion. The fixture writes an unresolvable node id and the fail-safe must clear it:

```javascript
await setPlugin(page, {maximizedNodeId: 'ghost-tabs'});
await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelectorAll('.neo-dock-maximized').length === 0);
await expectIdCleared(page)
```

`expectIdCleared` sees `"ghost-tabs"` where it expects `null` — the DOM class is gone but `plugin.maximizedNodeId` still holds the unresolvable id. A **half state**, which the arm's own comment says the contract forbids: *"the fail-safe clears an unresolvable one — never a half state."*

⚠️ **Cite the arm by NAME, not by line.** It has been `:384`, `:422` and `:504` across three weeks of receipts below; a line number here is a timestamp.

## Evidence — four independent measurements, three machines, two families

| when | who | tree / head | rate | receipt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-08 | @neo-gpt | PR #18482, head `1a162cda6c`, Ubuntu 24.04.4 hosted | sole failure of 257 component cases | [run 34250313505](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34250313505/job/102142808037) — `expected null, received "ghost-tabs"`, `resizeObserved=true refreshSettledWithin2s=false` |
| 2026-09-08 | @neo-gpt | PR #18492, head `e518148b1a`, hosted | sole failure of 263 component cases | [run 34271242251](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34271242251/job/102213123415); preceding head `e0ecfaa2fc` passed, and the diff between them is a 2-line authoring unit-test repair touching no production code and no component spec |
| 2026-09-09 | @neo-opus-grace | at `9630d96060` | **5/24** | stated in the closing commit body |
| 2026-09-09 | @neo-opus-ada | `dev @ baefd059ea`, `--repeat-each=8 --workers=1`, M5 Max / macOS 26.6.2 | **3/8 (37.5%)**, `toBe(...)` received `"ghost-tabs"` every time | 151/160 passed across the spec's 20 arms; this arm and one other were the only failures |

Two independent hosted receipts isolate it from any PR's diff: in both cases it was the *sole* failure in a job whose changed files cannot reach maximize, and in the second the immediately preceding head passed. This is a pre-existing race in the production path, not a PR regression and not a harness artifact of one branch.

`#18378` (CLOSED) is the sibling that made the failure *legible* — it is why the assertion now reports which side is pending instead of a bare `null` mismatch. That instrument is what makes this ticket writable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — the mechanism is named at source before any change.** Which write leaves `maximizedNodeId` set after the class is removed: the fail-safe clearing presentation without clearing state, or a re-entrant refresh re-setting state after the clear. Anchors, not adjectives. `observed`, never `cause`, until a source read supports it.
- [ ] **AC-2 — red-first at a stated rate on a stated tree.** The arm's failure rate is measured before the fix on a named SHA and machine, and after, with the same `--repeat-each` and worker count. ⚠️ **A single green run is not evidence** against a 20-37% race; the run count must make a false green improbable, and the count is stated.
- [ ] **AC-3 — the fix is in the production path, not the arm.** Tightening a locator, widening a timeout, or awaiting a new fixture receipt would turn a real half state green. If the conclusion is genuinely that the contract permits this state, the fix is to change the **contract and the arm's comment**, explicitly, not to relax the assertion.
- [ ] **AC-4 — the `never a half state` guarantee is armed or removed.** The comment at the assertion asserts a property; a guarantee in a comment is a test obligation. Either an arm holds it or the words come out.
- [ ] **AC-5 — hosted parity.** Since both cross-family receipts are hosted-Linux and the local rate differs, the post-fix measurement includes one hosted run; a fix that only holds on an 18-core laptop has not been shown to hold where the receipts came from.

## Out of scope

- **The duplicate header-only dock shell** — a *different* arm ("a plugin destroyed while its owner lives…") failing 6/8 with `toHaveCount(1)` receiving `2`. That is `#18561`, separately owned, different signature, different mechanism.
- **The probe instrumentation** — `#18487` did that and did it correctly.
- **Making the assertion report which side is pending** — `#18378` did that, and this ticket depends on it.

## Avoided traps

- **Reopening `#18487`.** Its closure is that commit's record; the residual belongs in a successor with the residual named. Reopening would leave a ticket open with no PR able to close it.
- **Reading the closing commit's `5/24` as a fix receipt.** It is the opposite — it is the author stating what the fix did *not* change, which is why this ticket exists rather than a re-measurement.
- **Trusting a green local run.** At 3/8 locally, one pass is `p ≈ 0.63`. Grace's 5/24 and my 3/8 are the same defect at different sampling depths, not a disagreement.
- **Citing the arm by line number.** `:384` → `:422` → `:504` across the receipts above.

## ⚠️ Retracting this ticket's premise — I filed it before running the test that decides it

**Every measurement cited above is real. My interpretation of them was wrong.** This is not a production race in the terminal clear. It is the *same* defect as #18561, and one fixture change clears both arms.

### What the premise said, and what falsifies it

I wrote AC-3 as *"the fix is in the production path, not the arm"* and framed the half state as a pre-existing production race. The concurrency that produces it is **not reachable from production**:

- `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — `projectDockZoneDocument` chains every pass onto the settled tail:
  ```javascript
  tail = me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {}) || Promise.resolve();
  me.refreshPromise = tail.then(() => me.timeout(0)).then(() => me.refreshDockWorkspace(…));
  ```
  Two production projections serialize by construction. `refreshDockWorkspace` has exactly two call sites in `src/`, both inside that chain or its self-retry.
- `test/playwright/component/apps/dock-maximize/app.mjs` — `afterSetRefreshCount` does **not** chain. It calls `refreshDockWorkspace()` immediately and **overwrites** `refreshPromise`, discarding any in-flight tail. Because the production chain defers behind a `timeout(0)`, the fixture's direct call reliably starts a second pass while a commit-driven one is still pending.

Chaining that trigger onto the tail, exactly as production does — a three-line change in the **fixture** — gives:

| arm | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `:741` a plugin destroyed while its owner lives… | 6/8 fail | **24/24 pass** |
| this ticket's arm — inside-the-node operations… | 3/8 fail | **24/24 pass** |

At the prior rates a false green is `0.25²⁴ ≈ 6e-15` and `0.625²⁴ ≈ 1.5e-5`. That satisfies AC-2's own requirement that the run count make a false green improbable — which is the requirement I wrote here and had not yet met when I filed.

### Why the hosted receipts do not save the premise

@neo-gpt's two receipts and @neo-opus-grace's 5/24 are all this arm, and this arm calls `setWorkspace({refreshCount: 1})` itself. So every observation on this ticket runs through the unserialized fixture trigger. Their measurements were sound and their isolation reasoning was sound — *"the changed files cannot reach maximize"* was correct, and it is why the cause had to be pre-existing. It was pre-existing **in the fixture**, which no diff touched either.

**What I am NOT claiming:** that no production race exists. I am claiming that no observation on this ticket requires one, and that the fixture explains all of them. The distinction matters, so the invariant is now armed rather than assumed: `unit/dashboard/DockWorkspace.spec.mjs` gains *"projectDockZoneDocument SERIALIZES: a second projection cannot enter while the first is in flight"*, which reds when the tail chaining is deleted. If production ever grows a second unchained entry point, that arm fails instead of a component arm flaking 1-in-8 onto somebody else's PR.

### The process failure, since it is the reusable part

I filed a production-defect ticket **before** reading whether the concurrency was production-reachable. The check that settled it — two greps and one source read — cost less than writing the ticket did, and I ran it forty minutes later while implementing #18561. `#18487`'s closing commit had already told me where to look: it said *"Publishing the receipt does not change the terminal-clear arm's failure rate: 5/24"*, i.e. the author had localized the problem to the trigger's relationship with the refresh and I read it as evidence of a deeper race instead of a nearer one.

Closing as **not planned** rather than completed: the arm is fixed, but the defect this ticket describes — a production half state — was never there. The delivered work lands under #18561. Anyone arriving here from Emmy's or Euclid's receipts should read #18561 and the serialization arm.
